h1: AI and digital consulting for New York companies, with one accountable lead
intro: 22 Signals provides the AI and digital consulting New York companies use when they want one team instead of ten suppliers: AI, cloud, data, websites, apps, SEO, paid media, video and 3D. A single Signal Lead owns your project, updates go into one shared channel, and every date we agree is written down.

sections.h: Why New York companies hire one team
p: A typical mid-sized company in Manhattan or Brooklyn has an IT provider, a web agency, an SEO freelancer, a media buyer, a video studio and now an AI consultant. Each is competent. None of them owns the outcome, so the CFO ends up project managing six invoices and the CMO spends Monday mornings reconciling six reports.

We cover AI, cloud and data, marketing, and video, animation and 3D in one team. That is the gap we fill for established businesses with 5 to 500 staff: one brief, one plan, one person to call. It is the kind of AI and digital consulting New York firms rarely find in one place.

list: AI consulting: a ranked list of AI uses, a roadmap and governance that fits NYDFS Part 500 and the city's rules on AI in hiring, then pilots your staff can test
AI automation: workflows that clear inboxes, read leases and invoices, and update the CRM, with a person approving anything risky
Business intelligence and data analytics: one checked set of numbers in Power BI, Looker Studio or Tableau, refreshed before the 9:00 meeting
Cloud consulting: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud set up so auditors can follow it, with monitoring that reaches a person while Manhattan sleeps
Web development: redesigns that keep rankings, sites built to WCAG 2.2 AA in a state that sees heavy accessibility litigation, and client portals
App development: iOS, Android and web apps for fintech, real estate, healthcare and retail, scoped in writing before a line of code
SEO and GEO: search across the five boroughs, plus how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Google AI Overview answers describe your business
Paid media (Google, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok ads): campaigns tracked to signed clients and revenue, with creative made in-house
Video production, animation and AI video: reels, explainers and editing teams, with AI performers labeled under New York's disclosure law
3D rendering: interiors and amenity floors for buildings still going up, plus product and packaging images for launches

sections.h: Industries we work with across the city
p: Financial services and insurance in Midtown, Hudson Yards and the Financial District. Media, publishing and advertising. Fashion and beauty, from the Garment District to SoHo. Hospitals, specialty practices and aesthetics clinics. Residential and commercial real estate. Law firms and professional services. Technology and SaaS companies around the Flatiron District and in Brooklyn. Each brings its own regulators, buyers and calendar, and our plans start from those rather than from a template.

list: The SHIELD Act: reasonable safeguards for private information about New York residents, plus a 30-day deadline to notify affected residents after a breach
NYDFS Part 500: cybersecurity rules for banks, insurers and other licensed firms, fully in force since November 2025
Local Law 144: independent bias audits and candidate notices for automated hiring tools used for jobs in the city
The synthetic performer law: conspicuous disclosure of AI-generated people in ads, in effect since June 2026
Attorney advertising and healthcare ad rules for law firms and clinics

sections.h: How a New York engagement runs
p: We work with New York companies remotely, with specialist teams behind one Signal Lead, and we have worked with more than 30 companies so far. A project starts with a 15-minute call, then discovery and a written roadmap within 5 to 7 days. Calls are booked at times that suit your team, and anything agreed on a call is confirmed in writing.
When a workshop, a site visit or a launch needs us in the room, we come to New York and plan that into the scope.

Right now, 10 of the businesses we work with sit in Google's top five for their main searches and show up in ChatGPT's answers. The work behind it is the same mix we offer here: technical fixes, accurate pages, consistent listings and steady monthly effort.

Every engagement follows the same four steps. We talk to understand the business and the people doing the work. We plan, with priorities, scope and dates in writing. We build, showing progress early and often. Then we grow it: measure, improve and add the next piece, or hand it over cleanly. The first step is a short fit check, not a pitch.

faqs.q: What do we get after the first call?
faqs.a: A short summary of what we heard and, after discovery, a written roadmap within 5 to 7 days. It lists the problems in order of value, the work we recommend, who owns each piece and the dates we commit to. You can take it to your leadership team before signing anything.

faqs.q: What kinds of New York companies do you work with?
faqs.a: Mostly established businesses with 5 to 500 staff in finance, media, fashion and beauty, healthcare, real estate, law and technology. We also work with founders and startups, but our process is built for companies with existing customers, data and teams.

faqs.q: Can one team really cover AI, cloud, marketing and video?
faqs.a: Yes, because each area has its own specialists, and one Signal Lead coordinates them for you. You get one plan and one point of contact, while the people doing the cloud work, the ad campaigns and the animation are each experts in that field.

faqs.q: How do you keep us updated during a project?
faqs.a: Your Signal Lead posts progress in one shared channel and sends a written report each month covering what shipped, what the numbers show and what comes next. Review calls are booked at times that suit you, and nothing reaches your team until it has been checked internally.

faqs.q: How much do your services cost?
faqs.a: It depends on scope: the services involved, the size of the work and whether we run things after launch. We do not publish prices. A 15-minute call is usually enough to tell you which factors apply and what a sensible first step looks like.
